Apple's annual September keynote is just weeks away, but according to all reports, one key product will be absent: the base iPhone 18. Here's when it's expected to launch.

The base iPhone 18 has been pushed to early 2027, as Apple adjusts its launch schedule.

The iPhone event is Apple's most important product launch of the year. If the company failed to release a new flagship iPhone in any given year, investors would be deeply concerned. This is one of the reasons Apple insists on keeping the iPhone launch schedule predictable.

With the exception of 2020, the event has been held in the first half of September every year. Typically, the new iPhone lineup includes the base model, two Pro versions, and a fourth option such as iPhone Air.

However, according to multiple reports dating back to May 2025, there will be no base iPhone 18 next month.

This move is highly unexpected. But it has now been confirmed by multiple sources, and it would be even more surprising if the base iPhone 18 ultimately did appear.

Why is there no iPhone 18 at this year's September event?

We don't know the exact reason, but possible explanations include:

  • Apple is deliberately spreading out iPhone launches to make room for more models, such as the iPhone Ultra this year.
  • Expected memory supply constraints are prompting Apple to make this adjustment to avoid a severe shortage.

Regardless of the reason, the iPhone 18's absence next month doesn't mean it's been cancelled. The base iPhone 18 will still launch, just delayed to early 2027.

According to rumours, three models will be released next month: the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra.

Then in early 2027, another three will follow: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2.

The timing is most likely no later than March. For reference, Apple launched the iPhone 16e in February and the iPhone 17e in March.

So if you want to buy Apple's next-generation iPhone but don't want to pay extra for a Pro or Ultra model, you'll just need to wait a few more months.

What do you think of Apple's rumoured major changes to its iPhone launch arrangements? Feel free to share in the comments section.
